issues.description: The template's oracle method for the multi-solution Grover exercise declares the `combinations` parameter as a single string (combinations: str), but both the problem statement and the solution implementation expect a list of bit-strings (list[str]). This inconsistency in the template's annotation and docstring is structural: the run/grover_circuit flow in the template supplies a list of combinations, and the solution's oracle expects a list. The incorrect annotation in the template can confuse students about the expected input type and leads to an inconsistent API between grover_circuit and oracle in the provided starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template oracle signature and its docstring to accept a list of bit-strings (combinations: list[str]) to match the problem statement and the solution. Ensure any references and type annotations in grover_circuit and run remain consistent with list[str].

issues.description: Mismatch in the 'oracle' method parameter type for the multi-solution Grover class: the template declares the parameter combinations as type 'str' while the problem statement and the solution implementation expect a list of bit-strings (list[str]). This inconsistent signature for the same conceptual parameter ('combinations') can confuse students implementing or overriding the oracle (inheritance/override expectations) and will likely cause type/usage errors when following the exercise instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template function signature to accept combinations: list[str] (matching the problem statement and solution). Also update the docstring/comments in the template to clearly state that 'combinations' is a list of bit-string solutions, so students can correctly implement and override the method.

issues.description: Exercise numbering and file/docstring labels for the QFT tasks are inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement refers to the QFT exercises as Exercise 6 and Exercise 7, while the template and solution source files are named ex1_qft.py and ex2_qft.py and their docstrings reference Exercise 1.1 / 1.2 and 2.1 / 2.2. This mismatch between exercise numbers in the problem text and file names/docstrings may confuse students about which file corresponds to which exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Align exercise numbering across artifacts: either rename the QFT files and update their docstrings to reference Exercise 6 and 7 (e.g., ex6_qft.py / ex7_qft.py) or update the problem statement to reference the current file names. Also update docstrings inside the files to mention the correct exercise numbers so students can unambiguously map problem text to the correct source files.
